Based on the provided healthcare Q&A matches, it appears that there is limited support for the possibility that occupational arsenic exposure could play a role in the development of diabetes mellitus among Swedish art glass workers. However, several other metallic compounds are also used in art glass production, which may increase the risk.

It is essential to note that active individuals with type 1 diabetes do not have a heightened Achilles tendon response to load, suggesting no increased risk of tendon injury. Moreover, European individuals with type 1 diabetes consume a high atherogenic diet and require more education on strategies to increase dietary fibre and reduce saturated fat.

Regarding high cumulative insulin exposure, these findings provide evidence that a high cumulative dose of regular insulin is a risk factor for atherosclerosis. Additionally, alcohol and drug use are important contributory factors to injury and poisoning deaths in young men.

The accuracy of FDG-PET in the diagnosis of cervical cancer patients with diabetes mellitus was not significantly reduced when compared to its accuracy in non-DM patients. However, ART patients may face higher C-section rates during their stage of delivery due to the effects of treatment on pregnancy outcomes.

Regarding T-cell deficiency and spatial learning ability following toluene exposure, these results indicate that T-cell deficiency may affect spatial learning performance after exposure to toluene. Finally, screening for gestational diabetes mellitus recommended by the International Association of the Diabetes and Pregnancy Study Groups is cost-effective and provides sensitive screening for individuals identified with GDM using postdelivery counseling and intervention.

In summary, while there are limited findings supporting a role of arsenic exposure in diabetes mellitus among Swedish art glass workers, other factors such as metallic compounds used in production, high cumulative insulin exposure, and increased risk after toluene exposure also need further investigation.
